strings.name: Xi Jinping
strings.role: CCP general secretary · President of China
strings.summary: After a career in local government and party leadership, Xi became CCP general secretary in 2012 and president in 2013. He pursued anti-corruption campaigns, centralized party-state power, poverty reduction and industrial policy while expanding China’s global economic and diplomatic role. Concentration of power, restrictions on expression and human rights in Xinjiang have drawn international criticism; inclusion and rating do not imply political endorsement.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: His leadership of China’s party and state, and his economic, technology, diplomatic and security policies, have substantial effects on the global order.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Chemical engineering, Tsinghua University (1979); in-service doctorate in law (2002)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Governance and industrial policy
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Anti-corruption, poverty reduction and industrial strategies under his leadership have wide domestic and global effects.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Diplomacy and contested governance
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: The Belt and Road and major-power relations are central policies; human rights and concentrated power also form part of his impact.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Follow-up to US–China summit
strings.timeline.event-01.text: China’s foreign ministry announced new understandings from talks with Donald Trump; subsequent plans are not treated as completed outcomes.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Third presidential term
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The National People’s Congress reelected him president and state Central Military Commission chairman.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Third term as general secretary
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The first plenum of the 20th CCP Central Committee elected him to continue as general secretary.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Presidential term limits removed
strings.timeline.event-04.text: A constitutional amendment removed the two-consecutive-term limit for the president and vice president.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Became president
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Assumed the presidency and later that year proposed the Silk Road Economic Belt and Maritime Silk Road.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Became CCP general secretary
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Elected at the 18th Central Committee’s first plenum; also became party Central Military Commission chairman.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Entered the top leadership
strings.timeline.event-07.text: After briefly leading Shanghai’s party organization, joined the Politburo Standing Committee.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Leadership in Fujian and Zhejiang
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Became acting Fujian governor in 1999, then governor; moved to Zhejiang in 2002 and held posts including party secretary.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Completed undergraduate studies
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Studied chemical engineering at Tsinghua, then worked in the State Council and Central Military Commission general offices.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Beijing
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Sent to Liangjiahe in Shaanxi in 1969; joined the CCP in 1974.
